A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CRM research. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable, allowing retained, relocated, and newly added material to be matched reliably.

before.justification: V1 reports original Best-of-N, beam-search, reinforcement-learning, and ablation results in Section 4 and the appendices.

after.justification: V2 retains those original experiments and adds multi-domain evaluation, additional baseline comparisons, generator-sensitivity results, and comparative data-efficiency experiments.

M1.justification: The conditional probability model, process reward log(1-h(t)), three training losses, and inference procedures remain unchanged. Appendix A.4 newly explains the already evaluated CRM+VR combination; it does not establish a changed algorithm.

E1.justification: V1 evaluates mathematical reasoning only. V2 adds training on MMLU-Pro-CoT-Train and evaluation on MMLU-Pro-CoT-Eval across biology, business, health, history, and physics (Section 4.5.4, Table 5), substantially broadening domain coverage while retaining the mathematical datasets.

E2.justification: V2 adds Major@N and oracle Pass@N comparisons to Table 1, R-PRM and GenPRM in Appendix H, and PRM to the data-efficiency comparison in Appendix J. It also adds verifier-only RL to Table 3 across six benchmarks, although VR already appeared in v1's Figure 1. These materially expand the evaluated comparison methods.

E3.justification: The original experimental protocols remain largely intact. Added settings include MetaMath-Mistral-7B generation, Pass@N evaluation, released-checkpoint comparisons, and PRM process-data subsampling. Section 4.5.3 corrects the stated ablation fractions from 0/25/50/75% to 0/10/25/50%, matching the unchanged Table 4; this does not establish rerunning the experiment.

E4.justification: Appendix I adds a substantive investigation of generator-dependent Best-of-N scaling using two generators and oracle candidate availability. Appendix J extends the CRM supervision ablation into a comparative data-efficiency study against PRM. The original reward-hacking, self-reflection, case-study, and reward-formulation analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions state that beam-search results average three random seeds and retain the same plus/minus reporting in Appendix B. The added experiments introduce no new run-count disclosures, uncertainty estimates, or significance-testing procedures.

E6.justification: Matched original scores and empirical plots remain unchanged, but v2 adds substantial new results. For example, Table 5 reports physics Best-of-64 accuracy of 66.4 for CRM versus 62.3 for PQM; Table 11 adds Best-of-16 scores of 51.2 for R-PRM and 55.2 for GenPRM alongside CRM's retained 56.4. Further additions cover verifier-only RL, majority/oracle selection, alternate generation, and PRM data budgets.

T1.justification: The probability definitions, assumptions, chain-rule decomposition, reward-shaping derivation, and loss equations are unchanged. The revised potential-function discussion is explanatory, and new Equation 17 documents the existing CRM+VR implementation rather than introducing a new theoretical result.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's three contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about conditional process-outcome modeling, credit assignment, cross-sample comparability, and resistance to reward hacking. The expanded experiments provide additional support without redefining these central claims.

C2.justification: Appendix I newly attributes differing Best-of-N scaling behavior to generator-dependent availability of correct candidates. Appendix J explains data efficiency through supervision propagating to earlier steps, while Section 4.5.4 interprets the new results as evidence of applicability beyond mathematics. These extend the interpretation without changing the central mechanism explanation.

D1.justification: Appendix A.4 specifies that CRM rewards every step and VR is added only at the final step. V2 also adds a project-site address and removes v1's promise to release code and checkpoints upon acceptance; the PDFs do not establish actual artifact availability. Existing hardware and training hyperparameters remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2 and Appendix H add focused positioning against reasoning-enhanced reward models, including R-PRM and GenPRM, and discuss their training and inference costs. Additional citations support potential-based shaping and introduce VersaPRM. The original novelty framing relative to PRM, PQM, and IPRM remains intact.

P1.justification: The main narrative and section order remain largely intact. V2 makes local grammatical edits, expands the potential-function explanation, adds Section 4.5.4 and Appendices H–J, introduces acknowledgments, and updates affiliation and conference text. The revision extends rather than extensively rewrites the document.

P2.justification: V2 adds substantial tabular displays for domain coverage, reasoning-enhanced baselines, generator behavior, oracle performance, and paired supervision budgets (Tables 5 and 11–14), and expands Tables 1 and 3. Figure 1a replaces probability-curve sketches with conditional-probability bars and a new legend. Existing empirical plots are retained and relocated.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially strengthens validation beyond v1's mathematics-only experiments and original comparator set. Five additional domains, reasoning-enhanced PRM comparisons, and quantitative verifier-only results address important gaps in applicability and comparative evidence. Generator-sensitivity and data-efficiency analyses further examine performance dependencies, while implementation clarification and corrected ablation percentages improve reproducibility. The added comparisons still lack uncertainty estimates and exact checkpoint identifiers, but the overall evidential gains are substantial.
